lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Concept model A: independence and the product rule

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Study both examples. The second one drops some of the wording of the first.

items.prompt: 30 people; 18 do A, 14 do B, 7 do both. Find P(A or B).
P(success) = 1/3 per trial, two trials. P(at least one)?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A survey table records: group X with 17 successes and 19 failures; group Y with 5 successes and 20 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 7/10, P(B) = 1/10, and P(A and B) = 7/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
No; the two events are mutually exclusive.

items.prompt: In a group of 35, 22 do activity A, 18 do activity B, and 10 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: An event has probability 4/6 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 25 successes and 11 failures; group Y with 14 successes and 4 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 5/10, P(B) = 9/10, and P(A and B) = 48/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.

items.prompt: In a group of 22, 7 do activity A, 11 do activity B, and 2 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: An event has probability 4/8 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 22 successes and 15 failures; group Y with 6 successes and 10 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
